# diagprint v0.4.0 — Diagnostic Intelligence

v0.4 evolves `diagprint` from a diagnostic presentation engine into a
structured diagnostic assistance system.

Diagnostics can now explain a problem, link to authoritative documentation,
propose structured edits, validate those edits against the current filesystem,
and optionally apply them.

## Highlights

### Structured Suggestions

Diagnostics can carry first-class suggestions with:

- explanations;
- documentation links;
- structured text edits;
- suggested follow-up commands;
- applicability classifications.

```rust
Suggestion::new("Enable chrono's serde feature")
    .applicability(Applicability::MachineApplicable)
    .documentation(
        DocumentationLink::docs_rs(
            "chrono",
            "latest",
            "",
        ),
    )
    .edit(...);
```

### Guarded Automatic Fixes

`Fixer` supports:

- previewing fixes;
- dry-run validation;
- automatic application;
- interactive application;
- optional backups.

Before editing a file, `diagprint` verifies that:

- the suggestion is machine-applicable;
- the edit range is valid;
- edit offsets are UTF-8 boundaries;
- edits do not overlap;
- the file still contains the expected original text.

Stale edits fail closed rather than guessing.

### Interactive Fix Workflow

```text
FIX  Enable chrono's serde feature
APPLICABILITY  machine-applicable
VERIFY  current file contents match the proposed edit
[A]pply  [S]kip  [D]ocs  [Q]uit >
```

If validation fails, the apply action is not offered.

### Documentation in the Terminal

The new optional `terminal-docs` feature can display linked documentation
directly in the terminal.

It provides:

- HTML-to-terminal conversion;
- Markdown rendering;
- extracted code examples;
- syntax highlighting;
- HTTP/HTTPS URL validation;
- document-size limits;
- terminal control-character sanitization.

Interactive fixes can open documentation with `[D]ocs`.

### Documentation Helpers

Convenience constructors are available for:

- docs.rs
- Rust compiler error documentation
- The Cargo Book

```rust
DocumentationLink::docs_rs("chrono", "latest", "");
DocumentationLink::rust_error("E0277");
DocumentationLink::cargo_book("reference/features.html");
```

### Suggested Commands Stay Advisory

A diagnostic may recommend:

```text
COMMAND cargo check
```

but `diagprint` never automatically executes suggested shell commands.

### Terminal Renderer

The existing themed diagnostic renderer now supports:

- `SUGGESTION`
- `PATCH`
- added lines
- removed lines
- `DOCS`
- `COMMAND`
- applicability
- fix status

Cybercore themes automatically map these new semantic roles into the active
Cybercore palette.

## Safety Hardening

v0.4 also adds:

- stale-edit rejection;
- stale-insert rejection;
- overlapping-edit detection;
- UTF-8 boundary validation;
- unique atomic temporary files;
- optional backups;
- remote terminal-control sanitization;
- remote-document size limits;
- offline terminal-doc rendering tests;
- action-aware interactive prompts.

## Feature Flags

| Feature | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `compression` | gzip and Zstandard report compression |
| `cybercore` | Cybercore theme integration |
| `terminal-docs` | terminal documentation and syntax highlighting |

All optional features remain disabled by default.

## Compatibility

There are no intentional breaking changes to the core v0.3 diagnostic
construction workflow.

v0.4 primarily adds new structured capabilities.

## Registry Status

GitHub releases are supported normally.

crates.io publication is intentionally disabled for this release while the
optional Cybercore integration is sourced from GitHub. Registry publishing
will be enabled after the matching Cybercore crate is available from the
target registry.

## Verification

The release gate covers:

- `cargo fmt`
- default-feature check
- default-feature Clippy with warnings denied
- default-feature tests
- rustdoc tests
- all-feature check
- all-feature Clippy with warnings denied
- all-feature tests
- all-feature rustdoc tests
- examples
- package-content inspection

## Next

Potential future work includes:

- `anyhow` integration;
- expanded `thiserror` integration;
- `tracing` integration;
- asynchronous report output;
- async documentation retrieval;
- richer unified diff presentation;
- additional renderers.
